_comment: TEMPLATE, not results. One entry per benchmark case. Fields capture everything a skeptic needs to reproduce a single case AND to know what its outcome would prove. No results are committed here; `expected_*` are the pre-registered expectations the harness will check against, not measurements. See docs/PUBLIC_BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md and docs/VALIDATION_HONESTY.md.

cases.label_basis: manual inspection of the base/head diff
cases.limitations: Reproduces one C3 reference break on one frozen SHA; not a real-world performance claim and not evidence the mechanism generalizes.

field_notes.head_sha_or_patch: Either a frozen head SHA in the same repo, or a path to a committed patch applied to base_sha. A patch is preferred when the change is synthetic/injected, so the mutation is auditable.
field_notes.expected_trigger: selected | not-selected — the trigger/selection layer: would revalidate re-check this claim when the watched source changes? Independent of truth.
field_notes.expected_truth: VERIFIED | BROKEN | ERRORED — the truth/alarm layer: GIVEN it is re-checked, what claim STATE should revalidate fold to? (A checker yields PASS/FAIL/ERROR; revalidate folds those to VERIFIED/BROKEN/ERRORED.) Only as strong as the checker backing the claim.
field_notes.layer: trigger | truth | both — which layer this case is designed to exercise.
field_notes.labeled_by/label_basis: Who decided the expected outcome and how — labels are human judgments and must be attributable.
